s.n: Formosa Cafe pork egg rolls with hot mustard
s.note: She is Lana Turner. Crisp rolls, pork and cabbage, Chinese mustard.
s.how: Stir-fry the pork until browned, add the wombok, carrot, spring onion and ginger and cook until wilted, then season with the soy and sesame oil and cool. Lay out a wrapper, add a spoon of filling, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing with a dab of water. Mix the mustard powder with a little cold water to a smooth, hot paste. Fry the rolls in oil at 180C in batches until deep golden, then drain. Serve hot with the mustard.

s.n: Frolic Room devilled eggs with paprika
s.note: Jack leaves his payola as a tip. Creamy yolks, mustard, cayenne, chives.
s.how: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water. Peel, halve lengthways and tip the yolks into a bowl. Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, cayenne and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pipe or spoon back into the whites, dust with paprika and top with chives.

m.n: Nite Owl chilli size with onions and cheddar
m.note: Exley takes the call to the Nite Owl. Grilled patty under beef chilli, cheese, onion.
m.how: Brown 400g of the mince with the onion and garlic, then add the chilli powder and cumin. Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer until thick and dark. Shape the rest of the mince into 4 thick patties, season and grill or pan-fry until browned and just cooked. Put each patty on a slice of toast, ladle over the chilli and top with cheddar and raw onion.

m.n: Ghost of Christmas Past ham steak with grilled pineapple
m.note: Bud pulls Santa's sleigh off the roof. Brown sugar glaze, pineapple, buttered greens.
m.how: Boil the potatoes until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain and toss with the butter. Mix the sugar, mustard, vinegar and cloves into a glaze. Sear the ham steaks in a hot pan, brush with glaze and turn until sticky and caramelised. Grill the pineapple in the same pan until charred, and serve on the ham with the potatoes and beans.

w.n: Rollo Tomasi's cherry pie a la mode
w.note: Rollo Tomasi, the one who got away. Lattice cherry pie, vanilla ice cream.
w.how: Line a 22cm pie dish with one sheet of pastry and chill. Warm the cherries, kept juice, sugar, cornflour and lemon juice, stirring, until thick and glossy, then stir in the almond and cool. Fill the pie, cut the second sheet into strips and weave a lattice over the top, then brush with egg. Bake at 200C until the pastry is deep golden and the filling bubbles. Cool a little and serve warm with ice cream.
shop: 2 x 680g jars pitted morello cherries, drained, 125ml juice kept@Pantry

d.n: All the whiskey in Ireland coffee
d.note: Dudley wouldn't trade places with Exley. Hot coffee, Irish whiskey, brown sugar, cream.
d.how: Warm 4 glasses with hot water, then tip it out. Stir a teaspoon of sugar and 40ml whiskey into each, then fill with coffee. Lightly whip the cream and float it over the back of a spoon.
